palette.notes: A community gallery, not one artwork. Its weekly challenges fix the canvas and the palette (the current one: a 70x100 portrait, 4 to 24 colours from one named 24-colour palette, no transparency, no animation), so a hard colour budget is the house discipline.

lighting: Not taught on the site pages; the FAQ points to a forum tutorial and to WIP critique threads instead.
silhouette: Not covered directly. The gallery's size rules (pieces over 100x100 need a preview of 100x100 or smaller, never scaled up) reward pieces that still read when tiny.

motion.timing: No timing guidance on the pages read; the current challenge forbids animation, so stills are judged on placement alone.

texture: Defines pixel art as the deliberate placement of single pixels; no filters or upscaled images in the gallery, so every pixel on screen is a pixel that was placed.
camera: No camera content. The challenge frames a fixed small canvas, which is a staging lesson: compose the whole idea inside one small, fixed frame.

acting.acts: No characters on the pages read; as staging it teaches that a piece must read at its smallest preview size and inside a fixed frame.

techniques: fixed canvas size and a capped palette (4-24 colours from one named palette) per piece
never scale images up; show art at 1x or clean integer scale
a 100x100-or-smaller preview must still read, so test the thumbnail
post work in progress for critique before calling it finished; ask specific questions
feel: hard canvas + hard colour cap + read-at-thumbnail test = deliberate, clean pixels
for_fred: Before a reel ships, check Fred and Pixie at their smallest on-screen size (a phone thumbnail) and at integer scale only: no smooth scaling, no blur, no off-grid rotation. Keep each scene under one fixed colour cap so the gags read, not the noise.
